title: How an apex locator finds the end
topic: The patient completes the circuit; ratio-type locators compare two AC signals, and that ratio drops sharply near the foramen.

claims.claim: The patient is the circuit: file, canal fluid, foramen, periodontal tissues, lip clip; dentin = insulator (drawn as a schematic)
claims.source: Nekoofar et al., Int Endod J 2006;39:595-609 (PMID 16872454), abstract ('dentine and cementum that are insulators'; a poor conductor rather than a perfect insulator, see Meredith & Gulabivala 1997); lip electrode: Nasiri & Wrbas, Saudi Dent J 2022;34:11-20 (PMID 35068894), full text

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: canal column drawn as a resistor that shortens as the file advances, root wall drawn as a capacitor; no component values
claims.source: Nekoofar et al., Int Endod J 2006;39:595-609 (PMID 16872454), abstract; Meredith & Gulabivala, Endod Dent Traumatol 1997;13:126-131 (PMID 9550026), abstract

claims.claim: 2 AC signals, 1 ratio; Root ZX: 0.4 + 8 kHz
claims.source: Ratio method: Kobayashi & Suda, J Endod 1994;20:111-114 (PMID 7996080), abstract; Root ZX frequencies: Oishi et al., J Endod 2002;28:361-364 (PMID 12026919), abstract. Toy model / schematic: the two waves are drawn 10:1, the real frequencies are 20:1

claims.claim: Fluid (saline, NaOCl) shifts both signals; the ratio barely moves. Toy model / schematic: wave sizes are illustrative
claims.source: Kobayashi & Suda, J Endod 1994;20:111-114 (PMID 7996080), abstract: quotient 'only negligibly influenced by the electrolyte'; 5.25% NaOCl more conductive than saline: Shin et al., Restor Dent Endod 2012;37:149-154 (PMID 23431125), abstract; NaOCl lowers canal resistance in vivo: Meredith & Gulabivala 1997 (PMID 9550026), abstract. Not on screen: blood in the canal did not change Root ZX accuracy in vivo (91.5% vs 86.2% within 0.5 mm, n.s.; accuracy-level evidence): Saatchi et al., Braz Dent J 2016;27:336-339 (PMID 27224570), abstract

claims.claim: Last ~1 mm: the ratio drops (in vivo, 7-21 canals per file position). Toy model / schematic: curve shape only, no values
claims.source: Rambo et al., Biomed Eng Online 2010;9:46 (PMID 20819212), full text (Table 2; n = 21 canals at 0 mm, 14 at -0.5 mm, 18 at -1 mm, 7 at -1.5 to -3 mm; custom research analyzer, canals irrigated with 2.5% NaOCl; 0 mm defined by a Root ZX reading plus a radiograph). The drawn curve follows the table's proportions: about 15% of the fall from -3 to -1 mm, 10% from -1 to -0.5 mm, 75% in the last 0.5 mm

Ounsi & Naaman, Int Endod J 1999;32:120-123 (PMID 10371907), in vitro, abstract ('should only be used to detect the foramen'); Martins et al., J Endod 2014;40:759-777 (PMID 24862702), systematic review, abstract ('detect the transition of the pulp to the periodontal tissue'); supporting: Rambo et al. 2010 (PMID 20819212), full text

J. Morita ROOT ZX II operation instructions (manufacturer document, not a PubMed source): 'The numerals on the meter gauge do not represent millimeters'; supported by Rambo et al. 2010 (PMID 20819212, full text: the ratio method cannot accurately measure distances between -3.0 and -0.5 mm from the foramen) and Ounsi & Naaman 1999 (PMID 10371907, abstract: the Root ZX 'is not capable of detecting the 0.5 mm from the foramen position')

claims.claim: Root ZX, in vivo: ~70-100% within ±0.5 mm; range of 16 studies
claims.source: Range of 16 in vivo abstracts, 1996-2023, not pooled; Root ZX family (Root ZX, Root ZX II, mini, Dentaport ZX), permanent teeth, hand files; most studies have 11-40 teeth. Reference point = major foramen, a point 0.5 mm coronal to it, or the minor foramen/constriction, depending on the study. Lowest 72%, Stöber et al., J Endod 2011;37:608-610 (PMID 21496657; reference 0.5 mm coronal to the major foramen); highest 100%, Vieyra et al., Int Endod J 2010;43:16-20 (PMID 20002800; 482 canals, 160 teeth, minor foramen) and De-Deus et al., J Endod 2023;49:487-495 (PMID 36848949; Root ZX II). Outside this scope: primary molars 65-69% (Beltrame et al., Int Endod J 2011;44:402-406, PMID 21219365); rotary NiTi files 50% (Siu et al., J Endod 2009;35:962-965, PMID 19567315). Full list in NOTES.md
Martins et al., J Endod 2014;40:759-777 (PMID 24862702), systematic review, abstract ('At least one radiographic control should be performed'); J. Morita ROOT ZX II operation instructions

claims.claim: History strip: 1918 Custer and 1962 Sunada (direct current), then AC impedance, then the ratio method (1994 = date of the J Endod paper)
claims.source: Custer, Dent Regist 1918;72:420-425 (PMID 33703181), full text; Sunada, J Dent Res 1962;41:375-387 (not in PubMed; record and secondary full text only); Nasiri & Wrbas, Saudi Dent J 2022;34:11-20 (PMID 35068894); Kobayashi & Suda, J Endod 1994;20:111-114 (PMID 7996080)

caption:
How does an apex locator find the end?
Patient = circuit: file > fluid > foramen > PDL > lip clip. Dentin acts as the insulator.
Ratio method (Root ZX: 0.4 + 8 kHz): 2 AC signals. Fluid shifts both; ratio barely moves, then drops in the last ~1 mm.
It senses the foramen region; marks ≠ mm. Root ZX family, permanent teeth, hand files, in vivo: ~70-100% within ±0.5 mm of each study's landmark (foramen, 0.5 mm short, constriction); 16 studies, not pooled. Confirm with a radiograph.
Schematic.
Refs: Nekoofar 2006, Ounsi 1999, Vieyra 2010 Int Endod J; Kobayashi 1994, Oishi 2002, Stöber 2011, Martins 2014 J Endod; Rambo 2010 Biomed Eng Online
